note: Quarterly data 2022Q4-2026Q3. 'verified' objects are hard sourced anchors (10-K/10-Q/8-K/investor-release figures, all cited in 19-act-ii-content-pack.md); all other quarterly cells are linear interpolation between anchor points and are marked estimate:true throughout -- treat every non-'verified' cell as ≈.
source: Company press releases/investor-relations pages (Core Scientific, IREN, Hut 8, Cipher Mining, CoreWeave), fetched directly where cited in 'verified'; interpolated quarters are directional shape, not individually sourced.

rivals.name: Core Scientific
profile: The largest miner/host in North America pre-2022; filed Ch.11 in Dec 2022 under crypto-winter debt, then emerged in Jan 2024 to become CoreWeave's largest hosting partner.

Went from a distressed 720MW miner to a ~590MW-targeted AI-hosting landlord, but its own EBITDA stayed negative through 2025 as colocation capex outran hosting revenue -- a cautionary case for over-committing to one hyperscaler-adjacent tenant.

key_moves.2022Q4: files Chapter 11 (20 Dec 2022); continues mining through bankruptcy
key_moves.2024Q1: emerges from Chapter 11 (24 Jan 2024) with ~$400M debt equitized; relists on Nasdaq
key_moves.2024Q4: CoreWeave exercises +112MW then +120MW options; $1.2B Denton TX expansion
key_moves.2025Q3: CoreWeave makes unsolicited ~$1B all-stock acquisition bid
key_moves.2025Q4: CORZ shareholders reject CoreWeave's ~$9B offer (30 Oct 2025); deal terminated; flags improper-capitalization restatement (no revenue/EBITDA impact)
key_moves.2026Q3: targeting ~590MW energized for CoreWeave by early 2027; new Hunt County TX (~430MW gross) and Dalton GA / Pecos TX sites

rivals.name: IREN (Iris Energy)
profile: A bitcoin miner (Childress TX; British Columbia) that announced a large AI-cloud pivot in 2023-24 but, as of its most recent reported quarter, still derives ~97% of revenue from mining -- the AI story is mostly pipeline/contracted-backlog, not yet realized revenue.
The $9.7B Microsoft deal (Nov 2025) is the single largest revenue-backlog event in this rival set relative to company size, and includes a rare 20% tenant prepayment.

key_moves.2023Q1: begins AI-cloud pivot alongside continued mining growth (Childress TX, British Columbia sites)
key_moves.2024Q4: Childress TX site being built out for eventual Microsoft capacity
key_moves.2025Q1: Q1 FY25: revenue $52.8M, Adj EBITDA $2.5M -- AI cloud still nascent
key_moves.2025Q4: $9.7B Microsoft contract (5yr avg term, 20% prepayment); targets $3.4B AI Cloud ARR by end of 2026 (~140k GPUs); Sweetwater Hub (2GW) substation energization targeted
key_moves.2026Q1: Q1 FY26 (reported quarter): revenue $240.3M (+355% YoY), mining $232.9M / AI Cloud $7.3M, Adj EBITDA $91.7M (38% margin), cash $1.8B, equity $2.876B

rivals.name: Hut 8
profile: Formed from the Feb 2023 merger of Hut 8 and US Bitcoin Corp, completed Nov 2023 -- the combined entity pursued mining, hosting AND a managed-infrastructure/HPC ambition simultaneously.

Its 2024 'profit' was almost entirely BTC fair-value accounting gains, not operating cash flow; 2025 flipped hard negative when BTC weakened, showing how exposed a miner-with-treasury business model still is even after signing a $9.8B AI lease.

key_moves.2023Q1: merger of equals with US Bitcoin Corp announced (7 Feb 2023)
key_moves.2023Q4: USBTC merger completed (30 Nov 2023), creating combined Hut 8 with expanded mining/hosting/HPC ambitions
key_moves.2024Q4: FY2024: revenue $162.4M, net income $331.4M (BTC FV gains), Adj EBITDA +$555.7M (gain-driven)
key_moves.2025Q2: 15yr, 245MW Fluidstack AI hosting lease at River Bend, Google-backed, ~$7B value
key_moves.2025Q3: American Bitcoin (majority-owned BTC-accumulation subsidiary, Trump-family-backed) completes Nasdaq listing
key_moves.2025Q4: FY2025: revenue $235.1M, net loss -$248M, Adj EBITDA -$135.4M; unrealized digital-asset losses $220M for the year ($401.9M in Q4 alone)
key_moves.2026Q2: Beacon Point Phase 1 commercialized: 352MW/15yr/$9.8B base ($25.1B incl. options) with an undisclosed 'high-investment-grade' tenant
key_moves.2026Q3: full 1GW Beacon Point campus fully contracted, $19.6B cumulative

rivals.name: Cipher Mining
profile: A pure-play Texas bitcoin miner (Odessa, Bear, Alborz sites) through 2024, then one of the fastest and most credit-enhanced AI pivots in the cohort in 2025: a Google-backstopped Fluidstack lease plus a separate AWS lease in the same year.

The Google backstop (warrants for ~5.4% of Cipher in exchange for guaranteeing Fluidstack's lease payments) is this pack's cleanest real-world example of the backstop mechanic converting a sub-investment-grade sub-tenant into bankable credit.

key_moves.2025Q3: signs 168MW/10yr Fluidstack AI hosting deal ($3B initial, ~$7B w/ extensions), Google backstops $1.4B for ~5.4% CIFR equity (25 Sep 2025)
key_moves.2025Q4: AWS 15yr/300MW lease (~$5.5B, phased delivery Jul-Dec 2026); additional 39MW/56MW Fluidstack tranches, Google backstop +$333M; completes $1.3B convertible note; cash jumps to $1.207B
key_moves.2026Q1: ~$11.4B contracted revenue backlog reported; Colchis site (West Texas) 1GW JV (~95% Cipher-owned); 1GW AEP direct-connect agreement targeting 2028
key_moves.2026Q3: S&P Global (Nov2025) projected revenue mix flipping to HPC-dominant within ~2 years -- on track

rivals.name: CoreWeave
profile: Not a bitcoin miner in spirit -- originated in 2017 as an Ethereum-mining operation ('Atlantic Crypto') but fully pivoted to GPU cloud by 2019-2022, years before the Merge. Included here as the sector's benchmark neocloud, the pattern every miner-pivot in this pack is chasing.

By FY2025 it had by far the largest revenue base ($5.1B) and largest debt load ($21.4B) of the cohort, and its GPU-backed DDTL financing (from SOFR+900-1000bps in 2023 down to SOFR+225bps investment-grade in 2026, then back up for weaker-tenant tranches) is this pack's cleanest real-world proof that debt spreads track counterparty credit quality more than calendar time.

key_moves.2017Q1: founded as 'Atlantic Crypto', an Ethereum-mining operation in New Jersey (background, pre-window)
key_moves.2019Q1: rebrands and pivots fully to GPU cloud compute after the 2018 crash (background, pre-window)
key_moves.2022Q4: Nvidia-backed; running large early Microsoft/OpenAI-adjacent contracts; no bitcoin-mining legacy remains
key_moves.2023Q3: first GPU-backed debt facility, $2.3B (Magnetar Capital & Blackstone), 3 Aug 2023 -- the sector's first major GPU-collateralized debt deal
key_moves.2024Q2: expanded debt facility to $7.5B (Blackstone/Magnetar); valuation reported at ~$19B (May 2024)
key_moves.2025Q1: IPOs 27-28 Mar 2025 at $40/share (below expected range), ~$1.5B raised; OpenAI contract $11.9B/5yr signed same month, later expanded by up to $6.5B
key_moves.2025Q4: FY2025: revenue $5.131B ('fastest cloud in history to $5B annual revenue'); RPO/backlog $66.8B (>4x where it began the year); active power capacity >850MW, contracted power ~3.1GW; now counterparty to all four major AI labs (Meta, Anthropic, OpenAI, Google); acquires Monolith and Marimo
key_moves.2026Q1: DDTL 4.0 closes ($8.5B, SOFR+225bps, first investment-grade-rated GPU-backed financing); Nvidia invests $2B (26 Jan 2026)
key_moves.2026Q2: Q1 2026 revenue guidance disappoints, stock -10% on the print (7 May 2026); DDTL 5.0 ($3.1B, SOFR+450bps, Ba2/BB+)
key_moves.2026Q3: DDTL 5.5 (~$2.6B) closes at a WIDER spread than DDTL 4.0 -- market pricing in tenant-credit and renewal risk even as the asset class matures

continuation_note_riot_marathon_bitfarms: By 2026, Riot Platforms stayed the most bitcoin-centric of the three, funding a 2026 AI/data-center expansion partly by selling BTC treasury (~9,665 BTC sold in H1 2026). Marathon Digital (MARA) pursued a similar hybrid stance, diversifying into HPC/AI hosting on the margin while keeping mining and treasury accumulation as its core identity. Bitfarms (BITF) was the most narrative-forward about its 'HPC & AI pivot' in 2025-26 coverage, with more analyst skepticism about whether it can convert the narrative into signed capacity at Cipher/Hut8 scale. By mid-2026, coverage grouped MARA, IREN and Riot as all facing 'fresh headwinds' in the AI pivot -- i.e. the market started questioning whether the AI-hosting story justified miners' valuations broadly. Source: kucoin.com news flash; Benzinga Jul 2026.
